question: Can a class-balanced, cross-validation-tuned ensemble of LightGBM and a balanced random forest beat a standard random forest on macro-F1 for predicting rare error categories in a small imbalanced tabular dataset?
method: Stratified 80/20 split (fixed seed); LightGBM grid over learning rate, leaves, L2 regularisation and min_child_samples chosen by stratified 5-fold CV on the training split; the ensemble weight between LightGBM and a class-balanced random forest chosen by out-of-fold CV on the training split; test macro-F1 for both models over three seeds.

dataset.name: OpenML Yeast (id 181), stand-in for DNSViz error logs

baseline: Default scikit-learn RandomForestClassifier (random_state=seed, all other defaults).
improved: Soft-voting ensemble of class-balanced LightGBM (hyperparameters chosen by 5-fold stratified CV macro-F1 on the training split) and a class-balanced random forest (balanced_subsample, 300 trees); mixing weight chosen by out-of-fold CV on the training split. No post-hoc probability calibration.
notes: Yeast is a stand-in: the DNSViz logs are not public, so results do not transfer directly to DNSSEC. Single stratified split with fixed seed; the rarest class has 4 training examples, so rare-class recall is noisy. Seeds vary model randomness only, not the split. Tuning and weight selection used CV on the training split only; the test split was scored once per model per seed. Isotonic calibration was dropped because with very few rare-class examples it suppressed rare-class predictions. Data loading uses openml's ARFF parser because scipy.io.arff in recent SciPy versions fails on bytes input.
